reason: I’ll strengthen the bone framework first. The picture shows spaces for mineral, and the mineral resists compression.
expectation: I expect the mineral to make the living bones harder while leaving the elbow joint in place.

alternatives.reason: Building the front muscle also matches a goal, but I want to strengthen the bones first.

effect: The mineral strengthened the bones while leaving the elbow movable. Now I need to build and attach both muscles.
reaction: It was satisfying to see how hard bone and a movable joint fit together.
reason: I’ll build the front muscle first; the cells and supporting tissue match the muscle-building goal.
expectation: I expect a front upper-arm muscle made from the cells and supporting tissue, though I’m not sure exactly how the tissue will fit.

alternatives.reason: The back muscle also needs building, but either side seems reasonable to start with.

effect: The front cells and supporting tissue formed the biceps, with tendon ends that can attach it to bones.
reaction: Seeing the separate cells join into fibres helped me understand how the muscle is built.
reason: I’ll build the back muscle too, since the chapter says muscles on opposite sides pull to move the elbow.
expectation: I expect a back upper-arm muscle with fibres and tendon ends, similar to the biceps.

alternatives.reason: I could attach the biceps now, but I want both muscles ready first.

effect: Both muscles are built; their tendon ends can now be attached on opposite sides of the elbow.
reaction: The matching cutaways made the front and back muscles easy to compare.
reason: I’ll attach the biceps first to work toward the goal of attaching both muscles.
expectation: I expect the biceps to attach across the front of the elbow, with its tendon ends connecting to bones.

alternatives.reason: I could attach the triceps first, but either order seems reasonable.

effect: The biceps is attached across the front of the elbow and its pull bends the forearm; the triceps still needs attaching.
reaction: The arrows made the connection between the muscle’s pull and bending clear.
reason: The only available combination attaches the triceps to complete the opposing muscle pair.
expectation: I expect the triceps to attach behind the elbow so it can pull the forearm straight.

effect: The completed arm shows how the two muscles pull from opposite sides to bend and straighten the elbow.
reaction: The two views made the opposing pulls clear and satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Attaching the triceps was most worthwhile because the two views showed how both muscles work together to move the elbow in opposite directions.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the back muscle repeated much of the front muscle’s result, though the matching pictures made them easy to compare.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected the supporting tissue around the muscle fibres to continue into the tendon ends.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless. The order of building and attaching the two muscles seemed like a choice of convenience rather than a meaningful difference.

continue.text: I would continue: seeing the separate parts become an arm with a clear movement made me curious about how another body system would fit together.
